title: Annotatio IV §.XVIII close: Ambrose — efficacious FIGURE; figurative words + real presence — stop before §.XIX
pass_a_gloss: The same elsewhere, in the book On the Eucharist ch. 4: Holy Ambrose (he says) does not intend to say that the bread becomes identically Christ’s body, but that it becomes His EFFICACIOUS FIGURE. Observe that Wycliffe sets an EFFICACIOUS FIGURE in the Supper, by which reason he contends both that the Institution words are to be understood figuratively and that meanwhile the most real presence of Christ’s body — from which all the Eucharist’s efficacy flows — is altogether to be admitted in the Sacred Eucharist.
pass_b_english: On the Eucharist ch. 4: Ambrose does not mean bread becomes identically Christ’s body, but His EFFICACIOUS FIGURE.
So Wycliffe holds both: Institution words figurative, and the most real presence of Christ’s body — source of all Eucharistic efficacy — fully admitted. Stop before §.XIX.
source_text: Idem alibi, libro de Eucharistia cap. 4. Sanctus (inquit) Ambrosius non intendit dicere, quòd panis fiat identicè corpus Christi, sed quod fiat ejus FIGURA EFFICAX. Observa, FIGURAM EFFICACEM Wiclephum in Cœna statuere, quâ ratione & verba institutionis figuratè intelligenda, & præsentiam interim corporis Christi realissimam, à qua omnis Eucharistiæ efficacitas promanat, in S. Eucharistia omninò admittendam esse, contendit.
